# READ DATA
Excluding "KTRL_01", "PLHC_01", and "PLHC_02"
```{r}
olli_data_raw <- read.xlsx("D:\\Olli\\All_PET_MRI_demo_data_from_R_2024-10-24 - Copy.xlsx")
olli_data <- olli_data_raw[!(olli_data_raw$ID %in% c("KTRL_01", "PLHC_01", "PLHC_02")),]
markus_mega_data <- read.xlsx("S:\\Neurologia\\MarkusM\\All_PET_MRI_demo_data_from_R_2025-03-13.xlsx")

# create new column with where all MS patients are labeled as "MS"
olli_data$Type_hc_ms[olli_data$Type == "HC"] <- "HC"
olli_data$Type_hc_ms[olli_data$Type != "HC"] <- "MS"
```

# FIX DUPLICATED IDs
```{r}

```

# CLEAN COLUMN NAMES

```{r}
names(olli_data) <- gsub("-", "", names(olli_data))
```

## lesion load classes
defined by highest and lowest third of values

##T1 lesion load
(lesion load is total lesion volume)
categories for highest, middle, and lowest third
```{r}
olli_data <- olli_data %>%
  mutate(Type_T1lesionload = ntile(T1hypolesionload, 3)) %>%
  mutate(Type_T1lesionload = case_when(
    Type_T1lesionload == 1 ~ "Low",
    Type_T1lesionload == 2 ~ "Mid",
    Type_T1lesionload == 3 ~ "High"
  ))
olli_data$Type_T1lesionload[olli_data$Type_hc_ms == "HC"] <- "HC"
```

# DEFINE FUNCTIONS
## boxplots_multiple_correction()
```{r}
boxplots_multiple_correction <- function(input_data,
                                        comparison_list = NULL,
                                        y_unit=" (DVR)",
                                        x_unit="",
                                        p_value_type="wilcox_p",
                                        bracket_nudge_y = 0.005,
                                        saving_folder = "Boxplots_DVR_test", #by default creates and saves to this testing folder
                                        saving = F, #to save or not to save
                                        group_column = "group", #choose grouping factor
                                        print_significant = F,
                                        printing = T,
                                        as_object = F,
                                        format_value = 3, #how many decimals to show minimum
                                        round_value = 3, #how many decimals to round to
                                        custom_order = NULL, #specify custom order for plotting
                                        text_size = 12,
                                        bracket_distance = 0.07,
                                        beeswarm_cex = 1.5,
                                        label_stats = F
                                        ) {

  # If custom_order is provided, convert group_column to factor with specified levels
  if(!is.null(custom_order)) {
    # Convert group column to factor with custom order
    input_data[[group_column]] <- factor(input_data[[group_column]], 
                                         levels = custom_order)
  } else {
    # If no custom order, sort alphabetically
    input_data <- input_data %>% arrange(!!sym(group_column))
    input_data[[group_column]] <- factor(input_data[[group_column]])
  }

  #list variables from DVR data you want to compare
  my_variables = list(names(input_data)[-which(names(input_data) == group_column)])

  for (my_variable in unlist(my_variables)) {

    # Drop rows with NA in the variable addressed by the current loop
    input_data_subset <- input_data[!is.na(input_data[my_variable]), ]

    # Get unique group values, respecting factor order
    group_values <- levels(input_data_subset[[group_column]])
    
    # Filter out groups with no data after NA removal
    group_values <- group_values[group_values %in% unique(input_data_subset[[group_column]])]

    # automatically collect all possible group wise comparisons based on group names
    if (length(group_values) > 2) {
      all_comparisons <- t(combn(as.character(group_values), 2))
      all_comparisons <- split(all_comparisons, seq(nrow(all_comparisons)))
    } else { #in case there are only 2 groups. combn() above cant handle it.
      all_comparisons <- list(c(group_values[1], group_values[2]))
    }

    # Only sort comparison pairs if no custom order is provided
    if(is.null(custom_order)) {
      all_comparisons <- lapply(all_comparisons, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
    }
    
    if(!is.null(comparison_list)) {
          if(is.null(custom_order)) {
            comparison_list <- lapply(comparison_list, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
          }
          all_comparisons <- all_comparisons[all_comparisons %in% comparison_list] #only keep the comparisons that are in the comparison_list
    }

    # precalculate comparisons between group means
    formula <- as.formula(paste0("`",my_variable,"`", " ~ ", group_column)) #predefined formula helps wilcox pick input from a list of column names
    # Filter to only include groups that are in the valid group_values
    valid_data <- filter(input_data_subset, !!sym(group_column) %in% group_values)
    stat.test <- filter(valid_data, !!sym(group_column) %in% unique(unlist(all_comparisons))) %>%
                 wilcox_test(formula)

    # Add t-test p-values to stat.test data frame
    # Create empty vector to store t-test p-values
    ttest_p_values <- numeric(nrow(stat.test))

    # Calculate t-test p-value for each comparison
    for (i in 1:nrow(stat.test)) {
      group1_data <- valid_data[valid_data[[group_column]] == stat.test$group1[i], my_variable]
      group2_data <- valid_data[valid_data[[group_column]] == stat.test$group2[i], my_variable]

      # Perform t-test and extract p-value
      ttest_result <- t.test(group1_data, group2_data)
      ttest_p_values[i] <- ttest_result$p.value
                                 }

    # Add t-test p-values to stat.test
    stat.test$ttest_p <- ttest_p_values

    # Add y position for pvalues
    stat.test <- stat.test %>% add_y_position(comparisons = all_comparisons) #calculate y positions for pvalues for plotting

    # Rename columns to match expected structure
    names(stat.test)[names(stat.test) == "group1"] <- "group1_orig"
    names(stat.test)[names(stat.test) == "group2"] <- "group2_orig"
    stat.test$group1 <- stat.test$group1_orig
    stat.test$group2 <- stat.test$group2_orig

    # Calculate x positions based on the order in group_values, not alphabetical
    stat.test$xmin <- match(stat.test$group1, group_values) 
    stat.test$xmax <- match(stat.test$group2, group_values)
    names(stat.test)[6:7] <- c("wilcox_statistic", "wilcox_p")

    if (length(group_values) > 2) {
      stat.test <- stat.test[,-c(8:9)] #drop adjusted values, will be done manually for more control over options
      row_pairs_list <- mapply(function(x,y) c(x,y), stat.test$group1, stat.test$group2, SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
    }

    # multiple comparison correction
    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) { #prevents errors when there are no valid comparisons
      stat.test$wilcox_p_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$wilcox_p, digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$wilcox_p_holmbonferroni <- p.adjust(stat.test$wilcox_p, method="holm") #less strict version of bonferroni correction
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg <- p.adjust(stat.test$wilcox_p, method="BH") #Benjamini-Hochberg Procedure aka False Discovery Rate
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg,digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded[stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded < 0.001] <- "<0.001"

      # Also add adjusted p-values for t-test
      stat.test$ttest_p_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$ttest_p, digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg <- p.adjust(stat.test$ttest_p, method="BH")
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg,digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value)
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded[stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded < 0.001] <- "<0.001"
    }

    # calculate n for each group in a way that ensures correct association with labels
    group_counts <- valid_data %>% 
      group_by(!!sym(group_column)) %>% 
      summarize(n = n())
    ns_named <- setNames(group_counts$n, as.character(group_counts[[group_column]])) # named vector for easier lookup

    # create another dataset for plotting to avoid errors from delayed evaluation
    plot_data <- valid_data
    plot_data$current_var_values <- valid_data[[my_variable]]
    
    # Calculate group-wise medians
    median_lookup <- plot_data %>%
      group_by(!!sym(group_column)) %>%
      summarize(median_value = median(current_var_values, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    # Create a vector to map group names to formatted median values
    medians_named <- setNames(
      format(round(median_lookup$median_value, digits = 2), nsmall = 2),
      as.character(median_lookup[[group_column]])
                             )
    
    if (label_stats == T) {  
    # Create custom labels for each group in advance
    group_labels <- sapply(group_values, function(g) {paste0(g, "\nmedian ", medians_named[g], "\nn=", ns_named[g]) })
    } else { group_labels <- sapply(group_values, function(g) { paste0(g,"\nn=", ns_named[g]) }) }
    
    # boxplot
    plot_boxplot <- ggplot(data = plot_data, aes(x = !!sym(group_column), y = current_var_values, fill = !!sym(group_column))) +
      geom_boxplot(linewidth = 1, fatten = 1, width = 0.6, outliers = F, color = "black") + #outliers are drawn by geom_beeswarm()
      geom_beeswarm(cex = beeswarm_cex) + #plot points on boxes without overlap or random jitter
      theme_bw() +
      xlab(paste0(x_unit)) +
      ylab(paste0(my_variable, y_unit)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.08))) + #expand y axis to prevent overlap with elements
      # use a function that looks up the correct n for each label
      scale_x_discrete(labels = group_labels) +
      theme(
        text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = text_size),
        axis.text = element_text(size = text_size, color = "black"),
        line = element_line(color = "black"),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1.5, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.5, color = "black"),
        legend.position = "none"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "gray90", "gray50", "gray30", "gray15")[1:length(group_values)]) 

    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) {
      plot_boxplot <- plot_boxplot +
        stat_pvalue_manual(data = stat.test,
                          label = p_value_type, #from which column to plot
                          xmin = "xmin",
                          xmax = "xmax",
                          y.position = "y.position",
                          tip.length = 0.01,
                          bracket.size = 1,
                          step.increase = bracket_distance, #increases the vertical distance of brackets
                          bracket.nudge.y = bracket_nudge_y,
                          color = "black",
                          size = text_size/.pt,
                          inherit.aes = F #local aesthetic fill=group in ggplot will break stat_pvalue_manual!
                          )
                             }

    # put the plot into the global environment
    if (as_object == T) {
      assign(paste0("plot_temp_", gsub(" ","",my_variable)), plot_boxplot, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }

    # print and save plots
    if (printing == T) {
      if (print_significant == T) {
        if(nrow(stat.test) > 0 && any(stat.test$wilcox_p <= 0.05)) {
          print(plot_boxplot)
        }
      } else {
        print(plot_boxplot)
      }
    }

    # Extract the test results for the current variable
    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) {
      boxplot_tests <- stat.test
      boxplot_tests$variable <- my_variable  # Add the variable name to track which test is for which variable

      # Append to the combined results data frame
      # check if all_boxplot_tests exists
      if (!exists("all_boxplot_tests")) {
        all_boxplot_tests <- boxplot_tests
      } else {
        all_boxplot_tests <- rbind(all_boxplot_tests, boxplot_tests)
      }
    }

    # save
    if (saving == T) {
      if (!dir.exists(saving_folder)) {
        dir.create(saving_folder, recursive = TRUE)
      }
      filename <- sprintf("%s.svg", gsub("[ \\(\\)\\.]", "", paste0("boxplot", my_variable)))
      ggsave(filename = here(saving_folder, filename), plot = plot_boxplot, units = "px", width = 1800, height = 1800)
    }
  }
  
  # Return all test results or NULL if none
  if (exists("all_boxplot_tests")) {
    return(all_boxplot_tests)
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
} #function end
```

## groupedboxplots_multiple_correction()
```{r}
groupedboxplots_multiple_correction <- function(input_data,
                                        comparison_list = NULL,
                                        y_unit=" (DVR)",
                                        x_unit="",
                                        p_value_type="wilcox_p",
                                        bracket_nudge_y = 0.005,
                                        saving_folder = "Boxplots_DVR_test", #by default creates and saves to this testing folder
                                        saving = F, #to save or not to save
                                        group_column = "group", #choose grouping factor
                                        print_significant = F,
                                        printing = T,
                                        as_object = F,
                                        format_value = 3, #how many decimals to show minimum
                                        round_value = 3, #how many decimals to round to
                                        custom_order = NULL, #specify custom order for plotting
                                        text_size = 12,
                                        bracket_distance = 0.07,
                                        beeswarm_cex = 1.5,
                                        label_stats = F,
                                        subgroup_column = "group"
                                        ) {

  # If custom_order is provided, convert group_column to factor with specified levels
  if(!is.null(custom_order)) {
    # Convert group column to factor with custom order
    input_data[[group_column]] <- factor(input_data[[group_column]], 
                                         levels = custom_order)
  } else {
    # If no custom order, sort alphabetically
    input_data <- input_data %>% arrange(!!sym(group_column))
    input_data[[group_column]] <- factor(input_data[[group_column]])
  }

  #list variables from DVR data you want to compare
  my_variables = list(names(input_data)[-which(names(input_data) == group_column)])

  for (my_variable in unlist(my_variables)) {

    # Drop rows with NA in the variable addressed by the current loop
    input_data_subset <- input_data[!is.na(input_data[my_variable]), ]

    # Get unique group values, respecting factor order
    group_values <- levels(input_data_subset[[group_column]])
    
    # Filter out groups with no data after NA removal
    group_values <- group_values[group_values %in% unique(input_data_subset[[group_column]])]

    # automatically collect all possible group wise comparisons based on group names
    if (length(group_values) > 2) {
      all_comparisons <- t(combn(as.character(group_values), 2))
      all_comparisons <- split(all_comparisons, seq(nrow(all_comparisons)))
    } else { #in case there are only 2 groups. combn() above cant handle it.
      all_comparisons <- list(c(group_values[1], group_values[2]))
    }

    # Only sort comparison pairs if no custom order is provided
    if(is.null(custom_order)) {
      all_comparisons <- lapply(all_comparisons, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
    }
    
    if(!is.null(comparison_list)) {
          if(is.null(custom_order)) {
            comparison_list <- lapply(comparison_list, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
          }
          all_comparisons <- all_comparisons[all_comparisons %in% comparison_list] #only keep the comparisons that are in the comparison_list
    }

    # precalculate comparisons between group means
    formula <- as.formula(paste0("`",my_variable,"`", " ~ ", group_column)) #predefined formula helps wilcox pick input from a list of column names
    # Filter to only include groups that are in the valid group_values
    valid_data <- filter(input_data_subset, !!sym(group_column) %in% group_values)
    stat.test <- filter(valid_data, !!sym(group_column) %in% unique(unlist(all_comparisons))) %>%
                 wilcox_test(formula)

    # Add t-test p-values to stat.test data frame
    # Create empty vector to store t-test p-values
    ttest_p_values <- numeric(nrow(stat.test))

    # Calculate t-test p-value for each comparison

      group1_data <- valid_data[valid_data[[group_column]] == stat.test$group1[i], my_variable]
      group2_data <- valid_data[valid_data[[group_column]] == stat.test$group2[i], my_variable]

      # Perform t-test and extract p-value
      ttest_result <- t.test(group1_data, group2_data)
      ttest_p_values[i] <- ttest_result$p.value
                                 }

    # Add t-test p-values to stat.test
    stat.test$ttest_p <- ttest_p_values

    # Add y position for pvalues
    stat.test <- stat.test %>% add_y_position(comparisons = all_comparisons) #calculate y positions for pvalues for plotting

    # Rename columns to match expected structure
    names(stat.test)[names(stat.test) == "group1"] <- "group1_orig"
    names(stat.test)[names(stat.test) == "group2"] <- "group2_orig"
    stat.test$group1 <- stat.test$group1_orig
    stat.test$group2 <- stat.test$group2_orig

    # Calculate x positions based on the order in group_values, not alphabetical
    stat.test$xmin <- match(stat.test$group1, group_values) 
    stat.test$xmax <- match(stat.test$group2, group_values)
    names(stat.test)[6:7] <- c("wilcox_statistic", "wilcox_p")

    if (length(group_values) > 2) {
      stat.test <- stat.test[,-c(8:9)] #drop adjusted values, will be done manually for more control over options
      row_pairs_list <- mapply(function(x,y) c(x,y), stat.test$group1, stat.test$group2, SIMPLIFY=FALSE)
    }

    # multiple comparison correction
    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) { #prevents errors when there are no valid comparisons
      stat.test$wilcox_p_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$wilcox_p, digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$wilcox_p_holmbonferroni <- p.adjust(stat.test$wilcox_p, method="holm") #less strict version of bonferroni correction
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg <- p.adjust(stat.test$wilcox_p, method="BH") #Benjamini-Hochberg Procedure aka False Discovery Rate
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg,digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded[stat.test$wilcox_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded < 0.001] <- "<0.001"

      # Also add adjusted p-values for t-test
      stat.test$ttest_p_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$ttest_p, digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value) #round values for plotting
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg <- p.adjust(stat.test$ttest_p, method="BH")
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded <- format(round(stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg,digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value)
      stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded[stat.test$ttest_p_benjaminihochberg_rounded < 0.001] <- "<0.001"
    }

    # calculate n for each group in a way that ensures correct association with labels
    group_counts <- valid_data %>% 
      group_by(!!sym(group_column)) %>% 
      summarize(n = n())
    ns_named <- setNames(group_counts$n, as.character(group_counts[[group_column]])) # named vector for easier lookup

    # create another dataset for plotting to avoid errors from delayed evaluation
    plot_data <- valid_data
    plot_data$current_var_values <- valid_data[[my_variable]]
    
    # Calculate group-wise medians
    median_lookup <- plot_data %>%
      group_by(!!sym(group_column)) %>%
      summarize(median_value = median(current_var_values, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      ungroup()
    
    # Create a vector to map group names to formatted median values
    medians_named <- setNames(
      format(round(median_lookup$median_value, digits = 2), nsmall = 2),
      as.character(median_lookup[[group_column]])
                             )
    
    if (label_stats == T) {  
    # Create custom labels for each group in advance
    group_labels <- sapply(group_values, function(g) {paste0(g, "\nmedian ", medians_named[g], "\nn=", ns_named[g]) })
    } else { group_labels <- sapply(group_values, function(g) { paste0(g,"\nn=", ns_named[g]) }) }
    
    # boxplot
    plot_boxplot <- ggplot(data = plot_data, aes(x = !!sym(group_column), y = current_var_values, fill = !!sym(subgroup_column))) +
      geom_boxplot(linewidth = 1, fatten = 1, width = 0.6, outliers = F, color = "black") + #outliers are drawn by geom_beeswarm()
      geom_beeswarm(cex = beeswarm_cex) + #plot points on boxes without overlap or random jitter
      theme_bw() +
      xlab(paste0(x_unit)) +
      ylab(paste0(my_variable, y_unit)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.08))) + #expand y axis to prevent overlap with elements
      # use a function that looks up the correct n for each label
      scale_x_discrete(labels = group_labels) +
      theme(
        text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = text_size),
        axis.text = element_text(size = text_size, color = "black"),
        line = element_line(color = "black"),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(linewidth = 1.5, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.5, color = "black"),
        legend.position = "none"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "gray90", "gray50", "gray30", "gray15")[1:length(group_values)]) 

    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) {
      plot_boxplot <- plot_boxplot +
        stat_pvalue_manual(data = stat.test,
                          label = p_value_type, #from which column to plot
                          xmin = "xmin",
                          xmax = "xmax",
                          y.position = "y.position",
                          tip.length = 0.01,
                          bracket.size = 1,
                          step.increase = bracket_distance, #increases the vertical distance of brackets
                          bracket.nudge.y = bracket_nudge_y,
                          color = "black",
                          size = text_size/.pt,
                          inherit.aes = F #local aesthetic fill=group in ggplot will break stat_pvalue_manual!
                          )
                             }

    # put the plot into the global environment
    if (as_object == T) {
      assign(paste0("plot_temp_", gsub(" ","",my_variable)), plot_boxplot, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }

    # print and save plots
    if (printing == T) {
      if (print_significant == T) {
        if(nrow(stat.test) > 0 && any(stat.test$wilcox_p <= 0.05)) {
          print(plot_boxplot)
        }
      } else {
        print(plot_boxplot)
      }
    }

    # Extract the test results for the current variable
    if (nrow(stat.test) > 0) {
      boxplot_tests <- stat.test
      boxplot_tests$variable <- my_variable  # Add the variable name to track which test is for which variable

      # Append to the combined results data frame
      # check if all_boxplot_tests exists
      if (!exists("all_boxplot_tests")) {
        all_boxplot_tests <- boxplot_tests
      } else {
        all_boxplot_tests <- rbind(all_boxplot_tests, boxplot_tests)
      }
    }

    # save
    if (saving == T) {
      if (!dir.exists(saving_folder)) {
        dir.create(saving_folder, recursive = TRUE)
      }
      filename <- sprintf("%s.svg", gsub("[ \\(\\)\\.]", "", paste0("boxplot", my_variable)))
      ggsave(filename = here(saving_folder, filename), plot = plot_boxplot, units = "px", width = 1800, height = 1800)
    }
  }
  
  # Return all test results or NULL if none
  if (exists("all_boxplot_tests")) {
    return(all_boxplot_tests)
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
} #function end
```

## table_means_etc()
```{r}
table_means_etc <- function(input_data,
                      parameter_list,
                      group_column, #choose grouping factor
                      format_value = 2, #how many decimals to show minimum
                      round_value = 2 #how many decimals to round to
                      ) {

table <- data.frame(
      parameter = character(),
      group = character(),
      n = numeric(),
      mean = numeric(),
      sd = numeric(),
      mean_sd = character(),
      median = numeric(),
      Q1 = numeric(),
      Q3 = numeric(),
      median_Q1_Q3 = character(),
      min = numeric(),
      masx = numeric(),
      min_max = character(),
      shapiro_p = numeric(),
      normality = character(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

for (loop_group in unlist(unique(input_data[[group_column]]))) {

for (loop_column in parameter_list) {
  collection <- input_data[input_data[[group_column]]==loop_group,]
  temp <- data.frame(
      parameter = NA,
      group = NA,
      n = NA,
      mean = NA,
      sd = NA,
      mean_sd = NA,
      median = NA,
      Q1 = NA,
      Q3 = NA,
      median_Q1_Q3 = NA,
      min = NA,
      max = NA,
      min_max = NA,
      shapiro_p = NA,
      normality = NA,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

  temp$parameter <- loop_column
  temp$group <- loop_group
  temp$n <- nrow(collection)
  temp$mean <- format(round(mean(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T),digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$sd <- format(round(sd(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T),digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$mean_sd <- paste0(temp$mean," (",temp$sd,")")
  temp$median <- format(round(median(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T),digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$Q1 <- format(round(quantile(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T)[2],digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$Q3 <- format(round(quantile(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T)[4],digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$median_Q1_Q3 <- paste0(temp$median," (",temp$Q1," - ",temp$Q3,")")
  temp$min <- format(round(min(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T),digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$max <- format(round(max(collection[[loop_column]],na.rm = T),digits=round_value),nsmall = round_value)
  temp$min_max <- paste0(temp$min," - ",temp$max)
  if (sum(!is.na(collection[[loop_column]])) > 2 && sum(!is.na(collection[[loop_column]])) < 5001) { #Shapiro-Wilk test is not valid for n>5000
    temp$shapiro_p <- format(round(shapiro.test(collection[[loop_column]])$p.value,digits=3),nsmall = 3)
    temp$normality <- ifelse(shapiro.test(collection[[loop_column]])$p.value < 0.05,"Not normal","Normal")
  } else {
    temp$shapiro_p <- NA
    temp$normality <- NA
  }
  table <- rbind(table,temp)
}

}

return(table)
} #function end
```

```{r}
table_sex_ratio <- function(input_data,
                      sex_column = "Gender",
                      group_column, #choose grouping factor
                      format_value = 1, #how many decimals to show minimum
                      round_value = 1, #how many decimals to round to
                      comparison_list = "empty"
                      ) {

table <- data.frame(
      group = character(),
      n = numeric(),
      n_f = numeric(),
      n_m = numeric(),
      f_n_ratio = numeric(),
      n_fn_ratio = character(),
      n_f_fn_ratio = character(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

for (loop_group in unlist(unique(input_data[[group_column]]))) {
  collection <- input_data[input_data[[group_column]]==loop_group,]
  temp <- data.frame(
      group = NA,
      n = NA,
      n_f = NA,
      n_m = NA,
      f_n_ratio = NA,
      n_fn_ratio = NA,
      n_f_fn_ratio = NA,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  
  temp$group <- loop_group
  temp$n <- nrow(collection)
  temp$n_f <- sum(collection[[sex_column]] == "f")
  temp$n_m <- sum(collection[[sex_column]] == "m")
  temp$f_n_ratio <- format(round(temp$n_f/temp$n*100,digits=round_value),nsmall=format_value)
  temp$n_fn_ratio <- paste0(temp$n," (",temp$f_n_ratio,")")
  temp$n_f_fn_ratio <- paste0(temp$n_f," (",temp$f_n_ratio,")")
  
  table <- rbind(table,temp)
}

# automatically collect all possible group wise comparisons based on group names
group_values <- unique(table$group)
if (length(group_values) > 2) {
  all_comparisons <- t(combn(as.character(group_values), 2))
  all_comparisons <- split(all_comparisons, seq(nrow(all_comparisons)))
} else { #in case there are only 2 groups. combn() above cant handle it.
  all_comparisons <- list(c(group_values[1], group_values[2]))
       }

all_comparisons <- lapply(all_comparisons, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
if(typeof(comparison_list) == "list") {
          comparison_list <- lapply(comparison_list, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
          all_comparisons <- all_comparisons[all_comparisons %in% comparison_list] #only keep the comparisons that are in the comparison_list
                                      }

fisher_results <- data.frame(matrix(ncol=length(all_comparisons),nrow=1))
for (loop_comparison in 1:length(all_comparisons)) {
  variable1 = all_comparisons[[loop_comparison]][1]
  variable2 = all_comparisons[[loop_comparison]][2]
  temp_contingency <- matrix(c(table$n_m[table$group == variable1],
                               table$n_m[table$group == variable2],
                               table$n_f[table$group == variable1],
                               table$n_f[table$group == variable2]),
                               nrow = 2,
                               dimnames = list(Group = c(variable1, variable2),
                                               Sex = c("Male", "Female")))
  names(fisher_results)[loop_comparison] <- paste0(variable1," vs ",variable2)
  fisher_results[1,loop_comparison] <- format(round(as.numeric(fisher.test(temp_contingency)["p.value"]),digits=3),nsmall=3)
                                                   }
table <- rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(t(table)),"parameter")
names(table) <- table[1,]
names(table)[1] <- "parameter"
table <- rbind(table[table$parameter == "n_f_fn_ratio",],table[table$parameter == "n",])
table <- cbind(table, rbind(fisher_results, rep(NA, nrow(table)-nrow(fisher_results))))

return(table)
} #function end
```

##correlation_analysis()
Calculates correlations between two variables within groups listed in group_column.
```{r}
correlation_analysis <- function(input_data, dependent, independent, method = "spearman", group_column = "group") {
    
  # create dataframe for saving results
  correlation_results <- data.frame(
    Variable1 = character(),
    Variable2 = character(),
    CorrelationCoefficient = numeric(),
    RawLower = numeric(),
    RawUpper = numeric(),
    P_value = numeric(),         
    AdjLower = numeric(),        
    AdjUpper = numeric(),
    Group = character(),
    n = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (group_loop in unique(input_data[[group_column]])[!is.na(unique(input_data[[group_column]]))] ) { #run once per group for within group correlations
    collection <- input_data %>% filter(!!sym(group_column) == group_loop)
    correlation_score <- corr.test(
      collection[independent], 
      collection[dependent], 
      method = method
    )
    for (i in seq_along(independent)) {
      for (j in seq_along(dependent)) {
        correlation_value <- correlation_score$r[i, j]
        
        raw_lower <- correlation_score$ci$lower[j]
        raw_upper <- correlation_score$ci$upper[j]
      
        p_value <- correlation_score$p[i, j]  
    
        adj_lower <- correlation_score$ci.adj$lower[j]  
        adj_upper <- correlation_score$ci.adj$upper[j]
        
        n_obs <- sum(!is.na(collection[[independent[i]]]) & !is.na(collection[[dependent[j]]]))  
        
        correlation_results <- rbind(correlation_results, data.frame(
          Variable1 = independent[i],
          Variable2 = dependent[j],
          CorrelationCoefficient = correlation_value,
          RawLower = raw_lower,
          RawUpper = raw_upper,
          P_value = p_value,       
          AdjLower = adj_lower,    
          AdjUpper = adj_upper,
          Group = group_loop,
          n = n_obs
        ))
      }
    }
  }

return(correlation_results)
} #end of function
```

```{r}
correlation_plots <- function(input_data,
                              input_analysis = significant_correlations,
                              y_data = "Variable2",
                              x_data = "Variable1",
                              x_unit = "", #gets added to axis title and filename
                              y_unit = "", #gets added to axis title and filename
                              saving_folder = "correlations_test", #by default creates and saves to this testing folder
                              saving = F, #to save or not to save
                              only_print = ".", #define this if you only want to print specific figures
                              only_save = ".", #define this if you only want to save specific figures
                              as_object = F,
                              printing = T,
                              group_column = "group",
                              format_value = 3, #how many decimals to show minimum
                              round_value = 3 #how many decimals to round to
                              ) {

  for (group_loop in unique(input_analysis$Group)[!is.na(unique(input_analysis$Group))]) { #runs once per group for within group correlations
  collection_correlations <- input_analysis %>% filter(Group == group_loop)
  for (v in 1:nrow(collection_correlations)) {

    # define variables for easier reading
    y_variable = collection_correlations[[y_data]][v]
    x_variable = collection_correlations[[x_data]][v]
    collection <- input_data %>% filter(get(group_column) == group_loop)
    collection <- na.omit(collection[c(y_variable,x_variable)]) #subset to be plotted, drop na containing rows
    R = format(round(collection_correlations$CorrelationCoefficient[v],digits = 2),nsmall = 2)
    p_val = format(round(collection_correlations$P_value[v],digits = round_value),nsmall = format_value)

    # plot
    plot_correlation <- ggscatter(collection,
                          y = y_variable,
                          x = x_variable,
                          add = "reg.line",
                          conf.int = F,
                          add.params = list(color = "black", fill = "gray85",linesize = 1.5, size = 1.5,
                          cor.method = "spearman"),
                          title = paste0("R = ", R, ", p = ",p_val,"\n","(",group_loop,", n = ",nrow(collection),")")
                          ) +
        xlab(paste0(x_variable," ",x_unit)) +
        ylab(paste0(y_variable," ",y_unit)) +
        theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
              plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5,vjust = -10),
              axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.5),
              axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.5)
              )
        # stat_cor(method = "spearman", size = 4, p.accuracy = 0.001)

    # print
    # only if variable names contain string in list provided by user
    if (printing == T) {
    if (any(sapply(only_print, function(pattern) grepl(pattern, paste0(y_variable))))) {
      if (as_object == T)  {
        print(plot_correlation) 
        assign(paste0("plot_temp_",gsub(" ","",
               paste0(collection_correlations$Variable1[v],"_vs_",collection_correlations$Variable2[v],"_",group_loop))),
               plot_correlation, envir = .GlobalEnv)
      }
      else {print(plot_correlation)}
    }
    }
      
    # save
    # only if variable names contain string in list provided by user
    if (saving == T && any(sapply(only_save, function(pattern) grepl(pattern, paste0(y_variable, x_variable)))) ){
    filename <- sprintf("%s.svg", gsub("\\.", "", paste0(y_variable,y_unit,"_vs_",x_variable,x_unit,"_",group_loop)))
    filename <- gsub(" ", "", filename)
    filename <- gsub("\\(", "", filename)
    filename <- gsub("\\)", "", filename)
    ggsave(filename = here(saving_folder, filename), plot = plot_correlation, units = "px", width = 1800, height = 1800)
    }
  }
}

} # end of function
```

## correlation_multiplots()
```{r}
correlation_multiplots <- function(input_data,
                              input_analysis = correlation_results,
                              y_data = "Variable2",
                              x_data = "Variable1",
                              x_unit = "", #gets added to axis title and filename
                              y_unit = "", #gets added to axis title and filename
                              saving_folder = "correlations_test", #by default creates and saves to this testing folder
                              saving = F, #to save or not to save
                              only_print = ".", #define this if you only want to print specific figures
                              only_save = ".", #define this if you only want to save specific figures
                              as_object = F, #save plot to global environment or not?
                              printing = T, #print or not?
                              group_column = "group", #which column do you want to use for grouping?
                              format_value = 3, #how many decimals to show minimum
                              round_value = 3 #how many decimals to round to
                              ) {

  # Extract unique variable pairs from the analysis
  unique_pairs <- input_analysis %>% 
    dplyr::select(all_of(c(x_data, y_data))) %>% 
    distinct()
  
  # For each variable pair
  for (p in 1:nrow(unique_pairs)) {
    
    # Define variables for easier reading
    y_variable <- unique_pairs[[y_data]][p]
    x_variable <- unique_pairs[[x_data]][p]
    
    # Filter data for this variable pair, dropping NA values
    plot_data <- input_data %>% 
      dplyr::select(all_of(c(group_column, y_variable, x_variable))) %>%
      na.omit()
    
    # Only proceed if we have data
    if(nrow(plot_data) > 0) {
      
      # Get correlation data for each group
      group_stats <- data.frame()
      
      for(grp in unique(plot_data[[group_column]])) {
        group_data <- plot_data %>% filter(get(group_column) == grp)
        if(nrow(group_data) >= 3) {  # Need at least 3 points for correlation
          corr_test <- cor.test(group_data[[x_variable]], group_data[[y_variable]], 
                               method = "spearman")
          
          group_stats <- rbind(group_stats, data.frame(
            Group = grp,
            n = nrow(group_data),
            R = format(round(corr_test$estimate, digits = 2), nsmall = 2),
            p_val = format(round(corr_test$p.value, digits = round_value), nsmall = format_value)
          ))
        }
      }
      
      # Initialize the plot with the first layer
      plot_correlation <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = x_variable, y = y_variable, color = group_column)) +
        geom_point() +
        geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
        xlab(paste0(x_variable," ", x_unit)) +
        ylab(paste0(y_variable," ", y_unit)) +
        theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
              plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
              axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.5),
              axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.5),
              legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.title = element_blank())
      
      # Add correlation statistics as a subtitle
      stat_text <- paste(
        sapply(1:nrow(group_stats), function(i) {
          paste0(group_stats$Group[i], ": R = ", group_stats$R[i], 
                 ", p = ", group_stats$p_val[i], ", n = ", group_stats$n[i])
        }),
        collapse = "\n"
      )
      
      plot_correlation <- plot_correlation + 
        labs(title = paste0(y_variable, " vs ", x_variable),
             subtitle = stat_text)
      
      # Print plot if it meets criteria
      if (printing == TRUE) {
        if (any(sapply(only_print, function(pattern) grepl(pattern, paste0(y_variable))))) {
          print(plot_correlation)
          
          if (as_object == TRUE) {
            assign(paste0("plot_temp_", gsub(" ", "", paste0(x_variable, "_vs_", y_variable))),
                   plot_correlation, envir = .GlobalEnv)
          }
        }
      }
      
      # Save plot if required
      if (saving == TRUE && 
          any(sapply(only_save, function(pattern) grepl(pattern, paste0(y_variable, x_variable))))) {
        filename <- sprintf("%s.svg", gsub("\\.", "", paste0(y_variable, y_unit, "_vs_", x_variable, x_unit)))
        filename <- gsub(" ", "", filename)
        filename <- gsub("\\(", "", filename)
        filename <- gsub("\\)", "", filename)
        ggsave(filename = here(saving_folder, filename), plot = plot_correlation, 
               units = "px", width = 1800, height = 1800)
      }
    }
  }
} # end of function
```

## williams test()
```{r}
table_williams_test <- function(input_data = correlation_results,
                      group_column, #choose grouping factor
                      format_value = 1, #how many decimals to show minimum
                      round_value = 1, #how many decimals to round to
                      comparison_list = "empty"
                      ) {
input_data$correlation <- paste0(correlation_results$Variable1," vs ",correlation_results$Variable2)
input_data
  
# automatically collect all possible group wise comparisons based on group names
group_values <- unique(input_data$Group)[!is.na(unique(input_data$Group))]
if (length(group_values) > 2) {
  all_comparisons <- t(combn(as.character(group_values), 2))
  all_comparisons <- split(all_comparisons, seq(nrow(all_comparisons)))
} else { #in case there are only 2 groups. combn() above cant handle it.
  all_comparisons <- list(c(group_values[1], group_values[2]))
       }

all_comparisons <- lapply(all_comparisons, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
if(typeof(comparison_list) == "list") {
          comparison_list <- lapply(comparison_list, sort) #sort each comparison pair alphabetically
          all_comparisons <- all_comparisons[all_comparisons %in% comparison_list] #only keep the comparisons that are in the comparison_list
                                      }

for (loop_correlation in unique(input_data$correlation)) {
  results <- data.frame(matrix(ncol=length(all_comparisons),nrow=1))
  for (loop_comparison in 1:length(all_comparisons)) {
    group1 = all_comparisons[[loop_comparison]][1]
    group2 = all_comparisons[[loop_comparison]][2]
    names(results)[loop_comparison] <- paste0(group1," vs ",group2)
    temp <- data.frame( #subset of data needed to make r.test
        correlation = loop_correlation,
        comparison = paste0(group1," vs ",group2),
        n1 = input_data$n[input_data$correlation == loop_correlation & input_data$Group == group1],
        coefficient1 = input_data$CorrelationCoefficient[input_data$correlation == loop_correlation & input_data$Group == group1],
        n2 = input_data$n[input_data$correlation == loop_correlation & input_data$Group == group2],
        coefficient2 = input_data$CorrelationCoefficient[input_data$correlation == loop_correlation & input_data$Group == group2],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    temp2 <- r.test(n = temp$n1, r12 = temp$coefficient1, n2 = temp$n2, r34 = temp$coefficient2) #williams test
    # cocor.indep.groups(temp$coefficient1, temp$coefficient2, temp$n1, temp$n2) #same result as williams test
    
    results[1,loop_comparison] <- format(round(as.numeric(temp2["p"]),digits=3),nsmall=3)
    results$correlation <- loop_correlation
    }#loop_comparison
      if(exists("results_all")) { 
      names(results_all) <- names(results)
      results_all <- rbind(results_all, results)
      } else { results_all <- results }
    }#loop_correlation
table <- results_all
return(table)
}#function end
```

DTI rows
```{r}
input_data <- olli_data
interesting_column <- "DMTlevelatimagingwithin2monthsbefore"
group_column <- "Type_hc_ms"
format_value <- 0 #how many decimals to show minimum
round_value = 0 #how many decimals to round to
comparison_list = "empty"

table <- data.frame(
      group = character(),
      n = numeric(),
      DMT0_n = numeric(),
      DMT1_n = numeric(),
      DMT2_n = numeric(),
      DMT0_percent = numeric(),
      DMT1_percent = numeric(),
      DMT2_percent = numeric(),
      DMT0_n_percent = numeric(),
      DMT1_n_percent = numeric(),
      DMT2_n_percent = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

for (loop_group in unlist(unique(input_data[[group_column]]))) {
  collection <- input_data[input_data[[group_column]]==loop_group,]
  temp <- data.frame(
      group = NA,
      n = NA,
      DMT0_n = NA,
      DMT1_n = NA,
      DMT2_n = NA,
      DMT0_percent = NA,
      DMT1_percent = NA,
      DMT2_percent = NA,
      DMT0_n_percent = NA,
      DMT1_n_percent = NA,
      DMT2_n_percent = NA,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  
  temp$group <- loop_group
  temp$n <- nrow(collection)
  temp$DMT0_n <- sum(collection[[interesting_column]] == 0)
  temp$DMT1_n <- sum(collection[[interesting_column]] == 1)
  temp$DMT2_n <- sum(collection[[interesting_column]] == 2)
  temp$DMT0_percent <- format(round(temp$DMT0_n/temp$n*100,digits = round_value),nsmall = format_value)
  temp$DMT1_percent <- format(round(temp$DMT1_n/temp$n*100,digits = round_value),nsmall = format_value)
  temp$DMT2_percent <- format(round(temp$DMT2_n/temp$n*100,digits = round_value),nsmall = format_value)
  temp$DMT0_n_percent <- paste0(temp$DMT0_n," (",temp$DMT0_percent,")")
  temp$DMT1_n_percent <- paste0(temp$DMT1_n," (",temp$DMT1_percent,")")
  temp$DMT2_n_percent <- paste0(temp$DMT2_n," (",temp$DMT2_percent,")")
    
  table <- rbind(table,temp)
}

table <- table[c("group","DMT0_n_percent","DMT1_n_percent","DMT2_n_percent")]
table <- rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(t(table)),"parameter")
names(table) <- table[1,]
names(table)[1] <- "parameter"
table <- table[-1,]
```

Two-way ANOVA
```{r}
columns_figure3 <- c("Brain_DVR","NAWM_DVR","WM_DVR","Cortical_GM_DVR","Thalamus_DVR")
columns_volumes <- 
columns_age <- c("Age_at_imaging","age_group","age_group_5yrs")
columns_subgroup <- c("Type_hc_ms","Type_T1lesionload_7cm3","Type_ventriclePF_212")

rm(results_all,results_interaction_all)
for (loop_variable_continous in columns_figure3) {
  for (loop_age in columns_age) {
    for (loop_subgroup in columns_subgroup) {
      # typical two-way anova
      formula_string <- paste0(loop_variable_continous," ~ ",loop_age," * ",loop_subgroup)
      current_formula <- as.formula(formula_string)
      two_way_model <- aov(formula = current_formula, data = olli_data)
      results <- tidy(two_way_model)
      results$continous <- loop_variable_continous
      rm(results_interaction)
      if(results$p.value[3] < 0.05) { 
        results_interaction <- results
        if (exists("results_interaction_all")) {results_interaction_all <- rbind(results_interaction_all, results_interaction) } 
        else { results_interaction_all <- results_interaction } 
        }
      if (exists("results_all")) { results_all <- rbind(results_all, results)} 
      else { results_all <- results }
  } #loop_subgroup
} #loop_age
} #loop_variable_continous
```

## linear model slopes by group
```{r}
olli_data$MS_gender <- paste0(olli_data$Type_hc_ms, "_", olli_data$Gender)
olli_data$Brain_DVR_ratio <- olli_data$Brain_DVR / olli_data$WholebrainvolumePF * 1000
olli_data$NAWM_DVR_ratio <- olli_data$NAWM_DVR / olli_data$WholebrainvolumePF * 1000
olli_data$Cortical_GM_DVR_ratio <- olli_data$Cortical_GM_DVR / olli_data$WholebrainvolumePF * 1000
olli_data$Thalamus_DVR_ratio <- olli_data$Thalamus_DVR / olli_data$WholebrainvolumePF * 1000

olli_data$Brain_DVR_density <- olli_data$Brain_DVR / olli_data$Wholebrainvolume
olli_data$NAWM_DVR_density <- olli_data$NAWM_DVR / olli_data$NAWMWMT2volume
olli_data$Cortical_GM_DVR_density <- olli_data$Cortical_GM_DVR / olli_data$CorticalGMvolume
olli_data$Thalamus_DVR_density <- olli_data$Thalamus_DVR / olli_data$Thalamusvolume

olli_data$DVR_ratio_sum <- olli_data$Thalamus_DVR_ratio + olli_data$NAWM_DVR_ratio + olli_data$Cortical_GM_DVR_ratio

columns_PFs <- c("WholebrainvolumePF","CorticalGMvolumePF","NAWMWMT2volumePF","ThalamusvolumePF")
columns_figure <- c("NAWM_DVR","Brain_DVR","Thalamus_DVR","Cortical_GM_DVR")
columns_test <- c("Brain_DVR_ratio","NAWM_DVR_ratio","Cortical_GM_DVR_ratio","Thalamus_DVR_ratio")
columns_test_2 <- c("Brain_DVR_density","NAWM_DVR_density","Cortical_GM_DVR_density","Thalamus_DVR_density")
columns_all <- c(columns_PFs,columns_figure,columns_test,columns_test_2)
columns_test_3 <- c("NAWM_DVR","NAWMWMT2volumePF","NAWM_DVR_density","NAWM_DVR_ratio")
columns_test_4 <- c("Brain_DVR","WholebrainvolumePF","Brain_DVR_density","Brain_DVR_ratio")
columns_test_5 <- c("NAWMFA","NAWMMD","NAWMAD","NAWMRD")
# columns_test <- c("DVR_ratio_sum")

# olli_data$Diseasedurationfromdiagnosis

for (loop_variable in columns_test_5) {
  # Create a local copy of the data for this iteration
  collection <- olli_data
  # collection[is.na(collection)] <- 0
  collection$current_variable <- (collection[[loop_variable]])  
  # collection <- collection[!is.na(collection$current_variable), ]
  # collection$current_variable <- log(collection$current_variable) # Log transform here
  collection <- collection[collection$Age_at_imaging < 71,]
  # collection <- collection[collection$Diseasedurationfromdiagnosis > 2,]
    # collection <- collection[collection$Type_hc_ms == "MS",]

  group_column <- "Type_hc_ms"
  explainer <- "Age_at_imaging"
  
  # Create formula (no parentheses needed)
  custom_formula <- current_variable ~ get(explainer)
  rm(slopes_list)
  
  for (loop_group in unique(collection[[group_column]])) {
    # Fit the models for MS and HC groups
    model1 <- lmrob(custom_formula, data = collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,])
    mdl_summary <- summary(model1)
    if (exists("slopes_list")) {
      slopes_list <- rbind(slopes_list, data.frame(
        group = loop_group,
        slope = mdl_summary$coefficients[2],
        p_value = mdl_summary$coefficients[2,4],
        r2 = mdl_summary$adj.r.squared,
        spearmam = cor.test(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$current_variable,
                    collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$Age_at_imaging, method = "spearman")$estimate,
        spearman_p = cor.test(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$current_variable,
                    collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$Age_at_imaging, method = "spearman")$p.value,
        n = nrow(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,])
        ))
        title_string <- paste0(title_string,"\n",
                               slopes_list$group[slopes_list$group == loop_group],
                               " slope = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$slope[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 6), nsmall = 6, scientific = F),
                               ", p = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$p_value[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 4), nsmall = 4, scientific = F),
                               ", r2 = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$r2[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 2), nsmall = 2, scientific = F),
                               ", spearman = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$spearmam[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 2), nsmall = 2, scientific = F),
                               ", p = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$spearman_p[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 4), nsmall = 4, scientific = F),
                               ", n =",
                               slopes_list$n[slopes_list$group == loop_group]
                               )
    } else {
      assign("slopes_list", data.frame(
        group = loop_group,
        slope = mdl_summary$coefficients[2],
        p_value = mdl_summary$coefficients[4],
        r2 = mdl_summary$adj.r.squared,
        spearmam = cor.test(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$current_variable,
                    collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$Age_at_imaging, method = "spearman")$estimate,
        spearman_p = cor.test(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$current_variable,
                    collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,]$Age_at_imaging, method = "spearman")$p.value,
        n = nrow(collection[collection[[group_column]] == loop_group,])
        ))
        title_string <- paste0(slopes_list$group[slopes_list$group == loop_group],
                               " slope = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$slope[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 6), nsmall = 6, scientific = F),
                               ", p = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$p_value[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 4), nsmall = 4, scientific = F),
                               ", r2 = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$r2[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 2), nsmall = 2, scientific = F),
                               ", spearman = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$spearmam[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 2), nsmall = 2, scientific = F),
                               ", p = ",
                               format(round(slopes_list$spearman_p[slopes_list$group == loop_group], digits = 4), nsmall = 4, scientific = F),
                               ", n =",
                               slopes_list$n[slopes_list$group == loop_group]
                               )
    }
  }
  
  

  # Create the plot
  p_compare <- ggplot(collection, aes(x = get(explainer), y = current_variable, 
                                color = get(group_column))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    # geom_smooth(method = "loess",span = 1.5, se = TRUE) +  # Simplified formula here
    geom_smooth(method = "rlm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE) +  # Simplified formula here
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Group") +
    labs(
      title = title_string,
      x = explainer,
      y = paste0("log(", loop_variable, ")")
    )
  
  assign(paste0("plot_temp_rlm_", gsub(" ", "", loop_variable)),
         p_compare, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  print(p_compare)
}
```

## DWPLOTS DVR

```{r}
## Define data subsetting
plotting_subset <- olli_data
plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Age_at_imaging < 71, ] # Age match controls with patients
# plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[scale(plotting_subset$NAWM_DVR) < 3 | scale(plotting_subset$Brain_DVR) < 3, ] # Remove outliers based on z-score
plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[scale(plotting_subset$Brain_DVR) < 3, ] # Remove outliers based on z-score

plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Gender == "f", ] # Subset to one gender
plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Type_benign != "Benign", ] # Subset to one gender

# plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Type_T1lesionload_7cm3 != "Low", ] # Subset to one gender



## Define variables and formulas
# List of dependent variables (region DVRs)
dependent_vars <- c("NAWM_DVR","Brain_DVR","Thalamus_DVR","Cortical_GM_DVR")
# plotting_subset$ventricle_volume_PF
# Define predictors

predictors <- "0 + age_group + Type_benign + Gender + BMI"
predictors_interaction <- "age_group * Gender + Type_benign + BMI"

predictors <- "0 + age_group + Type_benign + BMI"
predictors_interaction <- "age_group * Type_benign + BMI"

# vif(model_test)

## PART 1: Simple models without interaction
# Create empty lists to store models and labels
simple_models <- list()
simple_labels <- c()

# Loop through dependent variables to create models
for (i in seq_along(dependent_vars)) {
  var_name <- dependent_vars[i]
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors))
  # model_formula <- as.formula(paste0(var_name," ~ ", predictors))

  
  # Create model and store in list
  model_name <- paste0("model", i)
  simple_models[[i]] <- lmrob(model_formula, data = plotting_subset)
  
  # Create label for the plot
  model_text <- paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors)
  r2_value <- round(summary(simple_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared, digits = 2)
  simple_labels[i] <- paste0(model_text, ", r2=", r2_value)
  
  # Print summary
  cat("Model", i, "Summary:\n")
  print(model_text)
  print(summary(simple_models[[i]])$coefficients)
  print(paste0("Adjusted r2 = ",summary(simple_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared))
  cat("\n")
}

# # Diagnostic plots for one model (can be changed to any model)
# hist(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))
# qqnorm(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))
# qqline(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))

# Create the first plot
plot1 <- dwplot(
  vline = geom_vline(xintercept = 0),
  whisker_args = list(size = 1),
  dot_args = list(size = 2),
  simple_models
) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = rev(simple_labels)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

## PART 2: Interaction models
# Create empty lists for interaction models and combined model data
int_models <- list()
int_labels <- c()
all_int_terms <- NULL

# Loop through dependent variables to create interaction models
for (i in seq_along(dependent_vars)) {
  var_name <- dependent_vars[i]
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors_interaction))
  
  # Create model and store in list
  lmrob_control <- lmrob.control()
  lmrob_control$max.it <- 1000
  lmrob_control$maxit.scale<-4000
  lmrob_control$k.max <- 4000
  
  model_name <- paste0("model", i + length(dependent_vars))
  int_models[[i]] <- lmrob(model_formula, data = plotting_subset)
  print(summary(int_models[[i]]))
  
  # Create label for the plot
  model_text <- paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors_interaction)
  r2_value <- round(summary(int_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared, digits = 2)
  int_labels[i] <- paste0(model_text, ", r2=", r2_value)
  
  # Print summary
  cat("Interaction Model", i, "Summary:\n")
  print(model_text)
  print(summary(int_models[[i]])$coefficients)
  print(paste0("Adjusted r2 = ",summary(int_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared))
  cat("\n")
  
  # Extract interaction terms and prepare for dwplot
  model_tidy <- broom::tidy(int_models[[i]]) |> 
    filter(grepl(":", term)) |> 
    mutate(model = paste0("Model ", i + length(dependent_vars)))
  
  # Combine with other models
  all_int_terms <- rbind(all_int_terms, model_tidy)
}

# Create the interaction plot
plot3 <- dwplot(
  all_int_terms,
  vline = geom_vline(xintercept = 0),
  whisker_args = list(size = 1),
  dot_args = list(size = 2)
) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = rev(int_labels)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

# Combine plots
plot_figure_X <- ggarrange(
  plotlist = list(plot1, plot3),
  ncol = 1,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = "AUTO"
)

# Display the combined plot
plot_figure_X

```

```{r}
  all_int_terms,
  vline = geom_vline(xintercept = 0),
  whisker_args = list(size = 1),
  dot_args = list(size = 2)
) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = rev(int_labels)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

# Combine plots
plot_figure_X <- ggarrange(
  plotlist = list(plot1, plot3),
  ncol = 1,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = "AUTO"
)

# Display the combined plot
plot_figure_X
```




## DWPLOTS PFs 
```{r}
## Define data subsetting
plotting_subset <- olli_data
plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Age_at_imaging < 71, ] # Age match controls with patients
plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[scale(plotting_subset$Brain_DVR) < 3, ] # Remove outliers based on z-score
# plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Gender == "f", ] # Subset to one gender
# plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[plotting_subset$Type_T1lesionload_7cm3 != "Low", ] # Subset to one gender


## Define variables and formulas
# List of dependent variables (region DVRs)
dependent_vars <- c("NAWMWMT2volumePF", "WholebrainvolumePF","ThalamusvolumePF","ventricle_volume_PF","CorticalGMvolumePF")

# Define predictors
predictors <- "Cortical_GM_DVR + Age_at_imaging + Type_hc_ms + BMI + Gender"
predictors_interaction <- "Cortical_GM_DVR * Age_at_imaging + Type_hc_ms + BMI + Gender"

## PART 1: Simple models without interaction
# Create empty lists to store models and labels
simple_models <- list()
simple_labels <- c()

# Loop through dependent variables to create models
for (i in seq_along(dependent_vars)) {
  var_name <- dependent_vars[i]
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors))
  
  # Create model and store in list
  model_name <- paste0("model", i)
  simple_models[[i]] <- lmrob(model_formula, data = plotting_subset)
  
  # Create label for the plot
  model_text <- paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors)
  r2_value <- round(summary(simple_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared, digits = 2)
  simple_labels[i] <- paste0(model_text, ", r2=", r2_value)
  
  # Print summary
  cat("Model", i, "Summary:\n")
  print(model_text)
  print(summary(simple_models[[i]])$coefficients)
  print(paste0("Adjusted r2 = ",summary(simple_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared))
  cat("\n")
}

# # Diagnostic plots for one model (can be changed to any model)
# hist(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))
# qqnorm(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))
# qqline(residuals(simple_models[[2]]))

# Create the first plot
plot1 <- dwplot(
  vline = geom_vline(xintercept = 0),
  whisker_args = list(size = 1),
  dot_args = list(size = 2),
  simple_models
) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = rev(simple_labels)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 3))

## PART 2: Interaction models
# Create empty lists for interaction models and combined model data
int_models <- list()
int_labels <- c()
all_int_terms <- NULL

# Loop through dependent variables to create interaction models
for (i in seq_along(dependent_vars)) {
  var_name <- dependent_vars[i]
  model_formula <- as.formula(paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors_interaction))
  
  # Create model and store in list
  model_name <- paste0("model", i + length(dependent_vars))
  int_models[[i]] <- lmrob(model_formula, data = plotting_subset)
  
  # Create label for the plot
  model_text <- paste0("log(", var_name, ") ~ ", predictors_interaction)
  r2_value <- round(summary(int_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared, digits = 2)
  int_labels[i] <- paste0(model_text, ", r2=", r2_value)
  
  # Print summary
  cat("Interaction Model", i, "Summary:\n")
  print(model_text)
  print(summary(int_models[[i]])$coefficients)
  print(paste0("Adjusted r2 = ",summary(int_models[[i]])$adj.r.squared))
  cat("\n")
  
  # Extract interaction terms and prepare for dwplot
  model_tidy <- broom::tidy(int_models[[i]]) |> 
    filter(grepl(":", term)) |> 
    mutate(model = paste0("Model ", i + length(dependent_vars)))
  
  # Combine with other models
  all_int_terms <- rbind(all_int_terms, model_tidy)
}

# Create the interaction plot
plot3 <- dwplot(
  all_int_terms,
  vline = geom_vline(xintercept = 0),
  whisker_args = list(size = 1),
  dot_args = list(size = 2)
) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = rev(int_labels)) +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 3))

# Combine plots
plot_figure_X <- ggarrange(
  plotlist = list(plot1, plot3),
  ncol = 1,
  nrow = 2,
  labels = "AUTO"
)

# Display the combined plot
plot_figure_X
```

arrange plots

```{r}
                           ncol = 1, 
                           nrow = 4,
                           labels = "AUTO"
                           )
plot_figure_X
```

# SIMILARITY ANALYSIS - MS INDIVIDUALS VS HC INDIVIDUALS

```{r}
similarity_analysis <- function(
  data = mtcars,             # Input data frame 
  input_columns = c("mpg","cyl","disp","hp"), # Vector of columns to use for determining similarity
  group_column = "vs",  # Column that defines patient vs control groups
  patient_value = 1,      # Value in group_column that identifies patients
  control_value = 0,      # Value in group_column that identifies controls
  age_var = "mpg",           # Variable to compare (can be any numeric column)
  distance_metric = "euclidean", # "euclidean", "cosine", or "manhattan"
  x_label = NULL,             # Variable to plot on x-axis (column in results), NULL for automatic
  y_label = NULL,             # Variable to plot on y-axis (column in results), NULL for automatic
  plot_title = NULL,        # Plot title (if NULL, will be auto-generated)
  include_id = FALSE        # Whether to include patient/control IDs in results table
) {
  
  # Dependencies
  required_packages <- c("dplyr","ggplot2")
  
  # Check for missing packages
  missing_packages <- required_packages[!required_packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]]
  if(length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  cat("Installing missing packages:",paste(missing_packages),"\n")
  install.packages(missing_packages, repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")} # Install missing packages
  
  require(dplyr)
  require(ggplot2)

  # Automatically set x_label and y_label based on age_var if not specified
  if (is.null(x_label)) {
    x_label <- paste0("Patient_", age_var)
  }
  
  if (is.null(y_label)) {
    y_label <- paste0("Matching_Control_", age_var)
  }
  
  # Determine column names for results
  result_cols <- c(x_label, y_label, "Distance")
  if (include_id && "ID" %in% names(data)) {
    result_cols <- c(result_cols, "Patient_ID", "Control_ID")
  }
  
  # Create empty results dataframe with the correct column names
  results <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = length(result_cols), nrow = 0))
  colnames(results) <- result_cols
  
  # 1. Split data into patients and controls
  patients <- data[data[[group_column]] == patient_value, ]
  controls <- data[data[[group_column]] == control_value, ]
  
  # Remove rows with NA in any input columns
  patients <- patients[complete.cases(patients[, input_columns]), ]
  controls <- controls[complete.cases(controls[, input_columns]), ]
  
  if (nrow(patients) == 0 || nrow(controls) == 0) {
    stop("No valid data after removing NA values in brain columns")
  }
  
  # 2. Normalize attributes to make them comparable
  normalize_data <- function(df) {
    df_normalized <- df
    for (col in input_columns) {
      df_normalized[[col]] <- scale(df[[col]])
    }
    return(df_normalized)
  }
  
  patients_norm <- normalize_data(patients)
  controls_norm <- normalize_data(controls)
  
  # 3. Create function to calculate distance using specified metric
  calculate_distance <- function(v1, v2, method) {
    if (method == "euclidean") {
      return(sqrt(sum((v1 - v2)^2)))
    } else if (method == "cosine") {
      similarity <- sum(v1 * v2) / (sqrt(sum(v1^2)) * sqrt(sum(v2^2)))
      return(1 - similarity) # Convert to distance
    } else if (method == "manhattan") {
      return(sum(abs(v1 - v2)))
    } else {
      stop("Invalid distance method. Choose 'euclidean', 'cosine', or 'manhattan'.")
    }
  }
  
  # 4. For EACH INDIVIDUAL patient, find most similar control
  for (i in 1:nrow(patients_norm)) {
    # Get this individual patient's profile
    p_profile <- as.numeric(patients_norm[i, input_columns])
    p_value <- patients_norm[i, age_var]
    p_id <- if ("ID" %in% names(patients_norm)) patients_norm$ID[i] else i
    
    # Calculate distance to EACH INDIVIDUAL control
    control_distances <- data.frame(
      Control_Value = controls_norm[[age_var]],
      Distance = NA_real_,
      Control_ID = if ("ID" %in% names(controls_norm)) controls_norm$ID else 1:nrow(controls_norm)
    )
    
    for (j in 1:nrow(controls_norm)) {
      # Get this individual control's profile
      c_profile <- as.numeric(controls_norm[j, input_columns])
      
      # Calculate distance between this patient and this control
      control_distances$Distance[j] <- calculate_distance(p_profile, c_profile, distance_metric)
    }
    
    # Find closest match for this patient
    best_match <- control_distances[order(control_distances$Distance), , drop = FALSE][1, ]
    
    # Create new row for results
    new_row <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = length(result_cols), nrow = 1))
    colnames(new_row) <- result_cols
    
    new_row[1, x_label] <- p_value
    new_row[1, y_label] <- best_match$Control_Value
    new_row[1, "Distance"] <- best_match$Distance
    
    if (include_id && "ID" %in% names(data)) {
      new_row[1, "Patient_ID"] <- p_id
      new_row[1, "Control_ID"] <- best_match$Control_ID
    }
    
    # Append to results
    results <- rbind(results, new_row)
  }
  
  # Add Similarity column for plotting
  results$Similarity <- 1/results$Distance
  
  # 5. Create and return the visualization
  # Generate plot title if not provided
  if (is.null(plot_title)) {
    cols_str <- paste(input_columns, collapse = ", ")
    if (nchar(cols_str) > 40) {
      cols_str <- paste0(substr(cols_str, 1, 37), "...")
    }
    var_name <- gsub("_", " ", age_var)
    plot_title <- paste0("Individual Brain Similarity by ", var_name, "\n",
                         "Using: ", cols_str)
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(results, ggplot2::aes_string(x = x_label, y = y_label, size = "Similarity")) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = plot_title,
                  x = gsub("_", " ", x_label),  # Make axis labels more readable
                  y = gsub("_", " ", y_label),
                  size = paste0("Similarity \n(", distance_metric, ")")) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  
  # Return both results and plot
  return(list(results = results, plot = p))
}

result <- similarity_analysis()
print(result$plot)



# subset input data

# plotting_subset <- plotting_subset[abs(scale(plotting_subset$Brain_DVR)) < 3, ] # Remove outliers based on z-score

  data = plotting_subset,
  age_var = "Age_at_imaging",
  input_columns = c("NAWM_DVR","Brain_DVR","Thalamus_DVR","Cortical_GM_DVR"),
  distance_metric = "euclidean"
  )
```
